analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces בְּרִיתִי (“my covenant”), the direct object of וַהֲקִמֹתִי (“I will establish”). The possessive suffix makes בְּרִיתִי definite.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks בְּרִיתִי as the object of וַהֲקִמֹתִי, “I will establish.” God establishes his covenant “with you” (אִתְּכֶם) and promises that floodwaters will never again cut off all flesh.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a first-person common singular possessive suffix, “my.”
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh

draft.change: Add Genesis 9:11 as evidence for the existing Hebrew sense “not” at word index 0. The article already cites this verse for the phrase לֹא … עוֹד.
draft.definition: לֹא negates a statement, including a statement about what will happen.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 9:11, לֹא precedes יִכָּרֵת in the promise that floodwaters will never again cut off all flesh.

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִכָּרֵת כָּל בָּשָׂר עוֹד, לֹא negates the cutting off of all flesh by floodwaters. עוֹד supplies “again,” giving the promise “and never again will all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ joins the covenant promise to the preceding clause. The negative particle לֹא negates יִכָּרֵת, “will be cut off.”
analysis.sense: Denies that a future event will occur.

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִכָּרֵת כָּל בָּשָׂר עוֹד, God promises that all flesh will never again be cut off by floodwaters. The parallel promise that no flood will again destroy the earth confirms the sense of perishing.
analysis.morphology: Niphal imperfect, third-person masculine singular, agreeing with the collective subject כָּל בָּשָׂר. The negation לֹא is a separate word.

analysis.evidence: כָּל בָּשָׂר means “all flesh.” The promise that floodwaters will never again cut off all flesh treats living creatures collectively.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with בָּשָׂר as its complement.

analysis.evidence: כָּל בָּשָׂר is the subject of יִכָּרֵת, “be cut off.” The covenant promises that floodwaters will never again wipe out all living creatures.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix. It follows construct כָּל and has collective reference.
analysis.sense: all flesh: every living creature; mankind

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִכָּרֵת כָּל בָּשָׂר עוֹד, לֹא negates יִכָּרֵת and עוֹד marks recurrence. The covenant promise is that never again will all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew adverb with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: (with a negative) no more, no longer, never again

draft.change: Add Genesis 9:11 as evidence for the existing Hebrew sense a-body-or-flow.
draft.definition: A body or flow of water, including the waters of a flood.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:11 identifies the waters by their construct complement הַמַּבּוּל and describes their destructive effect.

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִכָּרֵת כָּל בָּשָׂר עוֹד מִמֵּי הַמַּבּוּל, the floodwaters are what could cut off all flesh. The parallel promise that no flood will again destroy the earth confirms the literal sense.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition מִן marks the cause of destruction. Its נ assimilates to the noun’s initial מ, producing the dagesh in מֵּי. The noun is masculine plural construct before הַמַּבּוּל.

draft.change: Link the occurrence to the existing flood sense. The current article already includes the Genesis 9:11 evidence.
draft.definition: An inundation in which rising waters cover the land.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:11 identifies the flood through the definite phrase מִמֵּי הַמַּבּוּל, “by the waters of the flood.”

analysis.evidence: In מִמֵּי הַמַּבּוּל, the article identifies the flood Noah survived. God promises that its waters will never again cut off all flesh. The next clause uses מַבּוּל without the article in the promise that there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the noun’s initial מ. The common noun מַבּוּל is masculine singular and absolute. It completes the construct phrase מִמֵּי הַמַּבּוּל, “by the waters of the flood.”

analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with שִׂיחַ.

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד מַבּוּל לְשַׁחֵת הָאָרֶץ, לֹא negates יִהְיֶה, and עוֹד marks recurrence. The promise is that there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew adverb without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: (with a negative) no more, no longer, never again

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד מַבּוּל לְשַׁחֵת הָאָרֶץ, “there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth,” מַבּוּל is the subject of יִהְיֶה. The earlier phrase מִמֵּי הַמַּבּוּל, “by the waters of the flood,” identifies the event whose recurrence the promise rules out.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: הָאָרֶץ is the object of לְשַׁחֵת. The promise that there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth parallels the promise that floodwaters will never again cut off all flesh.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ introduces the Piel infinitive construct שַׁחֵת.

analysis.evidence: הָאָרֶץ is the object of לְשַׁחֵת, “to destroy.” The promise that a flood will never again destroy the earth parallels the promise that floodwaters will never again cut off כָּל בָּשָׂר, “all flesh.” This scope supports the sense “earth” as a whole.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute. אָרֶץ is the pausal form of אֶרֶץ at verse end.
